title: A behavioral model of rational choice
authority: Simon (Nobel 1978) founded bounded rationality; this is the paper that replaced the omniscient economic actor with a cognitively limited chooser.
caveats: Satisficing as a term appears in Simon 1956 (Psychological Review 63(2):129-138). Descriptive model, not an empirically tested effect size; later work (Schwartz et al. 2002 maximizer scale) operationalized it with mixed results. Bibliographic details not re-confirmed by search this session (search budget exhausted); DOI removed.

title: Designing organizations for an information-rich world
container: Computers, communications, and the public interest
authority: Simon, Nobel laureate and cognitive scientist; this chapter is the origin of the attention economy idea.
caveats: A conceptual essay with no experiments. Page range from memory; confirm before citing pages. Bibliographic details not re-confirmed by search this session (search budget exhausted); DOI removed.

title: Judgment under uncertainty: Heuristics and biases
authority: Founding paper of the heuristics and biases program by two of the most cited decision researchers; Kahneman won the 2002 Nobel in economics.
caveats: Anchoring is robust and replicates widely; representativeness and availability are descriptive labels that critics (Gigerenzer) call vague. Specific numbers come from small student samples. Bibliographic details not re-confirmed by search this session (search budget exhausted); DOI removed.

title: Prospect theory: An analysis of decision under risk
authority: One of the most cited papers in economics; defines reference dependence and loss aversion.
caveats: Core patterns replicated across countries (Ruggeri et al. 2020, Nature Human Behaviour). Loss aversion as a general law is contested (Gal and Rucker 2018, Journal of Consumer Psychology 28(3):497-516). Bibliographic details not re-confirmed by search this session (search budget exhausted); DOI removed.

title: The framing of decisions and the psychology of choice
authority: Source of the Asian disease problem; the canonical demonstration that logically equivalent descriptions change choices.
caveats: Gain/loss framing replicates but effects are typically smaller than the original; moderated by wording and context (Kuhberger 1998 meta-analysis). Bibliographic details not re-confirmed by search this session (search budget exhausted); DOI removed.

title: Do defaults save lives?
authority: Columbia decision scientists; the most cited demonstration of default effects in public policy.
caveats: Country comparisons are correlational and measure registration, not actual donation; actual donation depends on health-system factors and family consent. Later work suggests opt-out registration rates overstate real effects. Volume/page details not confirmed this session; DOI and page range removed.

title: When and why defaults influence decisions: A meta-analysis of default effects
authority: Peer-reviewed meta-analysis of 58 studies by leading default researchers.
caveats: Authors include the originators of default research; heterogeneity is large and two studies show negative effects. Reported publication-bias checks were limited.

title: When choice is demotivating: Can one desire too much of a good thing?
container: Journal of Personality and Social Psychology
authority: Peer-reviewed in the top social psychology journal; the origin of the jam study.
caveats: The supermarket study was not cleanly replicated and the meta-analysis of Scheibehenne et al. 2010 found a mean effect near zero. Treat as a hypothesis about conditions, not a law. Bibliographic details not re-confirmed by search this session (search budget exhausted); DOI removed.

title: Can there ever be too many options? A meta-analytic review of choice overload
authority: Meta-analysis of 50 experiments from a Max Planck group; the standard skeptical reference on choice overload.
caveats: Chernev et al. 2015 argue that moderators were not modeled adequately and the effect is real under certain conditions.

title: Choice overload: A conceptual review and meta-analysis
authority: Peer-reviewed meta-analysis from a leading consumer psychology journal; the main rebuttal and refinement of Scheibehenne et al.
caveats: Authors previously argued choice overload is real; heterogeneity remains large. Moderators were coded post hoc.

title: The effectiveness of nudging: A meta-analysis of choice architecture interventions across behavioral domains
container: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
authority: Largest nudge meta-analysis to date, published in PNAS.
caveats: Maier et al. 2022 and Szaszi et al. 2022 show the headline effect shrinks sharply after correcting for publication bias.

title: No evidence for nudging after adjusting for publication bias
container: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
authority: Peer-reviewed reanalysis letter in PNAS by meta-science methodologists.
caveats: The authors' own rejoinder concedes the finding is 'undecided' overall, not evidence of absence; Data Colada criticized pooling heterogeneous interventions.

title: RCTs to scale: Comprehensive evidence from two nudge units
authority: Berkeley economists analysing every trial of two major US nudge units, a rare unbiased sample.
caveats: Outcomes are mostly take-up and compliance in government settings; generalization to learning apps is indirect.

title: Dark patterns at scale: Findings from a crawl of 11K shopping websites
container: Proceedings of the ACM on Human-Computer Interaction (CSCW)
authority: Princeton computer scientists; first large-scale measurement of dark patterns on the web.
caveats: Covers shopping sites only; automated detection finds a lower bound; counts instances not harm.

title: Shining a light on dark patterns
authority: University of Chicago law scholars; the key experimental evidence that dark patterns work and who they harm.
caveats: US online samples with a hypothetical-feeling service; page range from memory. Volume/page details not confirmed this session; DOI and page range removed.

title: Sludge audits
authority: Co-author of Nudge and former head of the US Office of Information and Regulatory Affairs.
caveats: Policy framework rather than empirical study; first online 2020. Sunstein's own earlier nudge claims are among those discounted by Maier et al.

title: Heuristic decision making
authority: Gigerenzer directs the Max Planck ABC group; this is the standard review of the fast-and-frugal program.
caveats: Advocacy for ecological rationality; the recognition heuristic and less-is-more claims have drawn serious critique (Pachur, Todd, Gigerenzer et al. debate in JDM 2011).
